environment: Manus Sandbox (ACE home), 8 cores Xeon 2.50GHz, ~24 GB RAM; llama.cpp b12316 (build 5d4c8eeb2), llama-bench -p 512 -n 128 -t 8, default repetitions; processes launched through the MCP door under sandbox-mcp.service with MemoryMax=21474836480 (20 GiB, raised by hub and verified 2026-11-13 17:36 WIB incl. a 2.5 GiB tenant allocation probe)
note: Sandbox CPU is heavily contended (bench processes averaged ~96-99% of ~1 effective core). Absolute t/s values are properties of THIS environment at THIS time, recorded as the mandate's load-burden measurement; they are not properties of the models.

attempts.outcome: Process group vanished during the pp512 phase between elapsed 20:51 (alive, RSS 15.6 GB) and ~18:57 WIB; buffered stdout lost, no result table produced.
Process group vanished again within ~2 minutes, after the table header flushed; the wrapper shell died with it (no BENCH_EXIT line written).

evidence: cgroup memory.peak == 21474836480 == MemoryMax exactly: the 32B working set saturates the 20 GiB ceiling; memory.events max counter rose 500791 -> 506865 across the attempts (allocations pressing the ceiling), while oom=0 and oom_kill=0.

No kernel OOM entry for either death (the only dmesg OOM is the 2026-11-13 16:39 kill of the earlier Llama bench under the old 1 GiB ceiling); systemd-oomd inactive; earlyoom running but logged no kill in the window; sandbox uptime continuous; sandbox-mcp.service not restarted (ExecMainStart 16:38, NRestarts=1).
dmesg shows virtio_mem hotplug activity (8 GiB chunks) at ~18:53-18:56 and ~19:03-19:04 WIB, overlapping both death windows.

Cause of the group kills: UNVERIFIED (platform-level action outside guest visibility is the remaining candidate). Two deaths on the largest model only; Llama (4.92 GB) and A3B (18.56 GB) completed through the identical route.
results.unblock: Raise sandbox-mcp.service MemoryMax toward the machine's ~24 GiB (hub/operator lever), or an operator-side explanation of the group kill; on either, the 32B bench is re-run with the identical protocol and this record is amended.
